Turner guru explicitly gives Kalasha gūrak heavy, Jaunsari garūo, Nepali garũo/garuṅo/garaũ/garũ and the Kotgarhi gɔrkɔ extension. The unprefixed survey forms match this family, with local vowel reduction, inflection and nasal extensions preserved. The Danuwar/Bote variants are a qualified comparison with the adjacent Nepali family, without claiming that their precise contact history is resolved.

Turner *udguru explicitly gives Kalasha agūrak, Bashkarik ugūr, Torwali ūgū, Palula úguro/úṅguro and Shina Kohistani hăgúro heavy. These prefixed northwestern forms fit that family rather than unprefixed guru. The local aspiration/frication and initial h are retained; Turner himself marks the explanation of emphatic h as uncertain.

Turner vahya gives Prakrit vojjha burden and Oriya bojha, Bengali bojhā and Hindi bojh load, with crossing from voḍhum. The survey uses this burden/weight word adjectivally for heavy. These are qualified regional family comparisons; Turner explicitly identifies Hindi diffusion of the noun into several western languages, so uninterrupted local inheritance is not asserted.
